geo.title: Get started
geo.body:
Connect midpoints of any quadrilateral (Varignon): always a parallelogram?

Goal: I can prove the triangle midsegment is parallel to the third side and half as long.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A midsegment of a triangle joins the midpoints of two sides.

Midsegment Theorem: a midsegment is parallel to the third side and half as long.

Proof: let M and N be the midpoints of AB and AC. Extend MN past N to P with NP = MN. Triangles AMN and CPN are congruent by SAS, so CP = AM = MB and angle NCP = angle A, so CP is parallel to MB. With one pair of opposite sides equal and parallel, MBCP is a parallelogram, so MP is parallel to BC and MP = BC. Then MN = (1/2)BC.

Join the midpoints of any quadrilateral's sides and you always get a parallelogram (Varignon's theorem): each side of it is parallel to a diagonal.
